evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for @gloria walking through the neon alley at night. I want the camera to slowly dolly in toward her face and end on a static close-up as she stops and turns toward the camera.
evals.expected_output: A prompt whose Camera block uses a slow dolly-in toward the named subject, with a shot size and angle, ending on a static lock.
expectations: The output uses 'dolly in' or 'push in' wording toward the named subject.
The output names which subject the camera follows (Gloria or @gloria).
The output gives a shot size for the move (e.g. close-up or medium close-up).
The output states where the move ends (e.g. a static lock) and does not add a second movement.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a dolly zoom on @marcus standing at the end of a long corridor. Keep his size constant while the background compresses closer behind him. I want a 50mm look with shallow depth of field.
evals.expected_output: A prompt whose Camera block names the dolly-zoom technique, preserves the subject's size, states whether the background moves closer or farther, and pairs the numeric lens value with a visible result.
expectations: The output names the dolly zoom technique explicitly.
The output specifies which subject's size must be preserved (Marcus or @marcus).
The output states whether the background moves closer or farther (compresses).
The output pairs any numeric lens value (e.g. '50mm') with a visible result such as shallow depth of field or bokeh, never a bare number (per the skill's advisory rule).
The output keeps simultaneous moves at or below 2.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a whip-pan transition at 5 seconds. The camera whips rapidly to the left, cuts when the foreground bookshelf fully covers the frame, then continues moving left at a similar speed in the next scene.
evals.expected_output: A prompt whose Camera block is a timestamped whip-pan transition including the trigger time, camera direction, occluding element, and the continuation after the cut.
expectations: The output uses 'At 5 seconds' or equivalent one-second timestamp syntax for the whip pan.
The output states the camera direction (rapidly to the left).
The output names the foreground occluding element that fills the frame (bookshelf).
The output specifies the continuation (continue moving left at a similar speed in the next scene).
The output keeps simultaneous moves at or below 2.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for an FPV drone shot flying through a ruined city: dive between the towers, bank hard right at the plaza, then climb over the cathedral. Fast speed.
evals.expected_output: A prompt whose Camera block uses first-person viewpoint and specifies the flight path through named spaces, the speed, and the turns or direction changes.
expectations: The output uses first-person view or FPV wording.
The output describes the flight path through named spaces (towers, plaza, cathedral).
The output specifies the speed (fast) of the flight.
The output specifies turns or direction changes (bank right, climb).
The output keeps simultaneous moves at or below 2.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a single continuous one-take shot: the camera follows a courier into a lobby, past the reception desk, into an elevator, and up to the 12th floor corridor, with no cuts.
evals.expected_output: A prompt whose Camera block is a one-take shot listing the subjects, spaces, and events the camera passes through in order.
expectations: The output uses one-take or single continuous take wording.
The output names the subject the camera follows (the courier).
The output lists the spaces the camera passes through in order (lobby, reception desk, elevator, 12th floor corridor).
The output orders the events (enters, passes, rides up, arrives) rather than presenting them unordered.
The output keeps simultaneous moves at or below 2.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a quiet moment between two old friends in a cafe. Use the Intimate Observer camera style: stay close to the subject, gentle handheld moves, capturing small gestures.
evals.expected_output: A prompt that selects exactly one camera style (Intimate Observer) and emits its camera-treatment block, with moves that stay near the subject.
expectations: The output selects exactly one camera style from the bank.
The output uses close-up or near-subject framing from the Intimate Observer block.
The output keeps the camera near the subject with gentle or handheld movement.
The output does not combine a second camera style in the same prompt.
The output keeps simultaneous camera moves at or below 2.

evals.prompt: Write a Seedance 2.5 prompt for a locked-off wide shot of a warehouse at dawn. The camera must not move at all; only the forklift moves within the frame.
evals.expected_output: A prompt whose Camera block uses static or locked-off wording, records the lock's static_reason (a user lock here), and does not rely on a camera_fixed generation parameter.
expectations: The output uses static or locked-off camera wording.
The output states that only the subject (the forklift) moves within the frame.
The output records why the camera is static (a user lock from the request), so the lock is a recorded choice.
The output does not add any camera movement.
The output does not rely on a camera_fixed parameter for the Seedance 2.5 tool and does not put generation parameters inside the prompt text itself.

evals.prompt: Write the Camera blocks for a 12-second Seedance 2.5 clip with three shots: a slow crane down on a kitchen, a slow push-in on a door handle, and a static low-angle close-up. Keep to the camera move rules.
evals.expected_output: Three Camera blocks, each with at most two moves for that shot, including a crane-down, a push-in and a static hold, each stating subject, start and end.
expectations: Each shot has its own Camera block with one primary move and at most one secondary move.
The clip as a whole is not capped at two moves because the moves belong to different shots.
Every move names the subject it follows and where it starts and ends.
The static hold is stated as a deliberate hold, not left as a missing camera line.

evals.prompt: Word the Camera block for an over-the-shoulder shot of Marta, seen from behind her brother Ben, in a medium close-up at eye level with a slow push-in.
evals.expected_output: One Camera block using the over-the-shoulder template: Ben's shoulder and head soft and dark on one side, Marta sharp facing the camera, medium close-up, one slow push-in with start and end.
expectations: The block names Ben as the soft foreground subject on a named side of the frame and Marta as the sharp featured subject.
The block gives the shot size and angle once, with one primary move that has a start and an end.
The block does not present over-the-shoulder wording as an official Seedance control.

evals.prompt: Write held (no camera move) Camera blocks for a three-shot of Ana, Bo and Cy at a bus stop, then a point-of-view shot from Ana's eyes of a letter in her hands.
evals.expected_output: A three-shot block naming left-to-right order and a point-of-view block from Ana's eyes showing her hands and the letter, each ending with a static hold, with advice to cover the POV with a looker and a reaction shot.
expectations: The three-shot names Ana, Bo and Cy in left-to-right order, all in focus, with a shot size.
The point-of-view block is first-person from Ana's eyes, shows the letter, and shows only the hands or limbs Ana would see of herself.
Each block states an explicit static hold rather than leaving the move out.
The output says the point-of-view shot should sit beside a shot of Ana looking and a reaction shot, or records why it stands alone.
